label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.72), PHQ-9 depression score (1.73), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.15) are all in the higher range, suggesting a co-occurrence of emotional distress across multiple dimensions. With 180 respondents in this cluster, the pattern points to a consistent association between heavy digital engagement and psychological burden among graduate-educated females.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital or internet usage (more than 5 hours)
Elevated loneliness despite high connectivity, suggesting possible social isolation or low-quality online interactions
Notable depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ~1.73) indicating persistent low mood or loss of interest
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean ~2.15) pointing to frequent worry or nervousness
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional distress
tone: Emotionally burdened, withdrawn, and anxiously preoccupied
